method.browser: Chromium 157.0.8103.78 (Playwright 1.63 headless), no hardware GPU: compositing and raster run in software on the CPU
method.cpuThrottle: CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate rate 4 (renderer main thread only)
method.window: 5 s per scenario after the effect is started (html.alive added at t0, as living.js would after load + idle)
method.passA: median of 3 runs: CDP Performance.getMetrics deltas (TaskDuration -> mainThreadMsPerSec, RecalcStyleDuration -> recalcStyleMs per second, RecalcStyleCount) plus PerformanceObserver long-animation-frame (>50 ms) and longtask; no tracing, no rAF probes
method.passB: 1 run with a light trace (devtools.timeline, blink.animations, toplevel, timeline.frame): Animation compositeFailed bitmask, per-thread busy time, Paint/UpdateLayoutTree counts, compositor DrawFrame rate
method.composited: true = every animation reported compositeFailed 0 AND style recalcs/paints per second stay at baseline; false = Blink reported a composite failure or per-frame style/paint

actions.pointer: Input.dispatchMouseEvent mouseMoved every ~16 ms across the bento cards (desktop, fine pointer)
actions.nav: click a same-origin link repeatedly (cross-document navigation)

method.lighthouse: Lighthouse 12.8.2 CLI, mobile form factor, default simulated throttling, median of 3, same Chromium; delta vs the baseline page (same content, static art)
caveats: Headless Chromium only. WebKit (all iOS browsers) and Gecko were not measured; WebKit does not composite animations on SVG child nodes and is more sensitive to backdrop-filter area.

softwareVizMsPerSec is CPU time of the GPU-process VizCompositorThread in software compositing. It is a RELATIVE indicator of compositor/GPU load (overdraw, blur), not a real-device number; with a hardware GPU it is far lower. It never counts toward TBT.
Main-thread numbers include input dispatch for pointer/scroll scenarios; compare against the matching baseline scenario (mainThreadMsPerSecVsBaseline).
For navigation scenarios getMetrics resets per document, so per-navigation trace numbers (trace.mainMsPerNav) are the comparable figures.

keyFindings: Lighthouse is blind to living motion. Every lab page scored 100 performance (median of 3), including SMIL (218 ms/s main thread), JS rAF attribute animation (207 ms/s), @property loops (152 ms/s) and filter:blur blobs that drop frames to 21-43 fps. TBT stayed 0-36 ms because the work comes as many small tasks, and the non-composited-animations audit misses SMIL, JS and blur cost. The QA motion-audit needs its own budget (below), not Lighthouse.

Start ambient loops after load + idle. Hero with loops running from first paint: TBT median 36 ms and main-thread work 387 ms; started after load + idle: TBT 0 and 329 ms (baseline 246 ms). LCP stays the H1 and Speed Index does not move either way.
Ambient transform/opacity loops on OUTER boxes are effectively free on the main thread: all safe ambient effects together cost 1.3 ms/s in steady state.

Scroll-linked CSS (scroll()/view()) composites, but Chromium still runs a main-thread style update on every scroll frame: +31 ms/s for hero parallax and +36 ms/s for 16 view() reveals at 4x. IntersectionObserver one-shot reveals cost about a third of that.
Never animate a registered custom property (@property) in a loop: 2 conic borders = 152 ms/s, 180 paints/s. A transform-rotated conic layer looks the same for 3.6 ms/s.

Blur cost is on the compositor, not the main thread: filter:blur blobs and backdrop-filter over animated layers look clean in main-thread metrics but multiply compositor work (4-7x) and drop frames. Pre-blurred gradients and glass only over static art.

On an <svg> layer box animate `transform` only. The independent `translate` property on an SVG element is not composited (SVGTargetHasIndependentTransformProperty): combining parallax-by-translate with drift-by-transform cost +97 ms/s.

Chromium 153 composites CSS transform/opacity animations on SVG child nodes (the inner-node control was cheap); SMIL and JS attribute animation are not composited at all. WebKit was not measured; keep the outer-box rule for cross-engine safety.

Filters on SVG tiles (map drop-shadow) are main-thread: +72 ms/s during a hover sweep with a filter transition, 76 ms/s as an ambient pulse. Use instant on/off for hover and an opacity-animated HTML glow box for the pulse (3.4 ms/s).

motionAuditBudgetProposal.note: Proposed for tools/motion-audit.mjs (qa), measured like this lab: Chromium, CDP CPU throttle 4x, 5 s windows, motion on.
motionAuditBudgetProposal.steadyStateIdleMainThreadMsPerSec: <= 10 after data-alive + 2.5 s (lab: all safe effects 1.3)
motionAuditBudgetProposal.scrollMainThreadMsPerSecOverStaticPage: <= +60 at 4x (lab: parallax +31, view() reveals +36, IO reveals +11; all-safe +131 fails this, so reveals must use IO)
motionAuditBudgetProposal.infiniteAnimationsCompositeFailed: 0 (trace Animation.compositeFailed); allow only transform and opacity in keyframes used by infinite animations
staticLintBans: @keyframes that animate a custom property, filter, backdrop-filter, stroke-dashoffset, width/height, top/left in an infinite animation
requestAnimationFrame loops that write styles or attributes
backdrop-filter on an element whose ancestor-stacking context or backdrop contains an infinite animation

thresholds.safe: composited, <= ~5 ms/s main-thread over baseline at 4x, 0 long frames, Lighthouse perf delta >= -1
thresholds.ration: bounded in time/area/count or interaction-only main-thread cost, or composited but heavy on the compositor
thresholds.avoid: continuous non-composited main-thread work (style+paint every frame) or a measurable Lighthouse loss

effects.name: Living layered SVG hero: 5 outer <svg> layer boxes drifting by transform (+2 firefly boxes by opacity)
effects.lighthouseNote: Perf 100 both ways. Starting the loops at first paint ("alive immediately") added TBT (median 36 ms) and ~60 ms more main-thread work than starting after load + idle (TBT 0); LCP (the H1) and Speed Index did not move.
effects.notes: 4.8 ms/s main thread vs 0.5 idle (+4.3), 0 long frames, 0 of 5 (0 of 7 with fireflies) animations failed to composite, ~1.4 paints/s (start only). Firefly boxes add nothing measurable on the main thread. Most of the 4.8 ms/s is the start-up (one style pass); in steady state the whole safe set of ambient loops together costs 1.3 ms/s (see the combined entry). The cost is on the compositor: 5 full-bleed layers at 112% width are ~250 ms/s of software-compositor CPU at 412 px and saturate it at 1440x900 (898 ms/s, 50 fps) in this GPU-less container; on real GPUs this is overdraw, not jank, but it is the reason to cap layer count and area. Test scene size: 7.6 KB raw / 1.9 KB gzip for 5 layers + 2 firefly boxes.
guidance: Animate only OUTER <svg> boxes (or HTML wrappers) with transform/opacity keyframes; one animation per box.
Keep it to 5-6 boxes; paint the sky gradient as the hero background (static), not as a drifting full-size layer.
Scene container: position:absolute; inset:0; overflow:hidden; contain:strict (or paint) sized to the hero, not the viewport.
Start after load + idle (data-alive), pause with animation-play-state when off-screen (IntersectionObserver) and on visibilitychange.
Never put backdrop-filter glass directly over the drifting layers (see glass entry).

effects.name: Scroll-timeline parallax (animation-timeline: scroll(root)) on the 5 hero layer boxes
effects.lighthouseNote: Lighthouse does not scroll, so only the load cost is visible (all-safe page, which includes a parallax wrapper).
effects.notes: Composited (0 of 5 failures) but Chromium still runs a style/animation update on the main thread for every scroll frame: 78 ms/s vs 47 ms/s for the same scroll on the static page (+31 ms/s, ~16 extra style recalcs/s, 0-1 long frames). Combining parallax via `translate` with the drift via `transform` on the SAME box breaks compositing for those 5 animations (5 of 10 failed: SVGTargetHasIndependentTransformProperty, because the layer box is an <svg> element) and costs +97 ms/s with ~78 recalcs/s.
guidance: Hero only, <=5 boxes, animation-range limited to the hero (0 to 100vh), inside @supports and gated by the motion policy (T4).

On an <svg> box animate only `transform`; the independent translate/rotate/scale properties are not composited on SVG elements. To combine parallax and drift, put parallax on an HTML wrapper and the drift on the inner <svg>.

effects.name: Contour stroke-dashoffset draw-in (12 map contour paths)
effects.lighthouseNote: In the all-safe page the 12 contour paths are what Lighthouse lists under non-composited animations (12 items) and most of its extra main-thread work; the score does not move.
effects.notes: Never composited (UnsupportedCSSProperty + TargetHasInvalidCompositingState): every frame is a style recalc plus a repaint of the SVG. Steady-state cost while drawing is ~118 ms/s with 120 paints/s for 12 paths (contour-loop); the 1.6 s one-shot averages 41 ms/s over a 5 s window and then drops to zero, with 0 long frames. Scroll-scrubbed with view() it costs +41 ms/s over plain scrolling (88 vs 47) and ~20 paints/s for as long as the map is in range.
guidance: One-shot, time-based, <=1.6 s, triggered once when the map enters view (IntersectionObserver adds a class) rather than scroll-scrubbed.
<=12 short paths with pathLength="1"; static drawn state under reduced motion and with no JS.
Never on the hero, never looping.

effects.name: Scroll reveals with view() timeline (opacity + transform, 16 targets)
effects.lighthouseNote: Lighthouse does not scroll; load cost only (all-safe page). Must never apply to the LCP element or above-the-fold content.
effects.notes: All 16 animations composited, but like scroll() parallax each scroll frame triggers a main-thread style update: 83 ms/s vs 47 ms/s on the static page (+36 ms/s mobile, +48 ms/s desktop), 0 long frames, ~3.7 paints/s. The same reveal done as a one-shot CSS transition triggered by an IntersectionObserver class (reveals-io) costs +11 ms/s mobile / +26 ms/s desktop over plain scrolling, about a third, because nothing is linked to scroll position after the element has appeared.
guidance: Prefer the one-shot version: an IntersectionObserver adds a class once (then unobserves) and a <=600 ms opacity/transform transition runs (T1). Hidden state only applies under html.alive, so no-JS and reduced motion always show content.
If view() is used, one reveal per section (the section wrapper), not every child: cost scales with the number of active scroll-linked animations.
opacity/transform only, short animation-range (entry 0% to cover 30%), inside @supports, off under the motion policy.
Never on the H1/LCP element or anything in the first viewport.

effects.name: Cursor spotlight (delegated rAF-throttled pointermove)
effects.lighthouseNote: Fine pointer only, so it never runs in a Lighthouse mobile run; JS ~0.3 KB.
effects.notes: Measured on desktop with the pointer sweeping the 6 bento cards at ~30-60 Hz. Custom-property version (--mx/--my set on the hovered card, radial-gradient ::before): 139 ms/s vs 79 ms/s for the same pointer sweep with no effect (+60 ms/s), ~29 style recalcs/s and ~59 paints/s. Transform version (a pre-rendered radial glow element per card moved with translate3d): +43 ms/s and ~1.6 paints/s. Only active while the pointer moves over a card; 0-1 long frames (same as the baseline sweep).
guidance: Prefer the transform version: one absolutely positioned glow child per card, moved with transform; no repaint.
If custom properties are used, set them on the hovered card only, never on :root or body (that restyles the whole document).
One passive listener on the grid, rAF-throttled, (pointer:fine) and motion-on only (T3).

effects.name: @property --angle conic-gradient border animation (ambient, 2 elements)
effects.lighthouseNote: Delta vs baseline; ambient loop started before load.
effects.notes: Animating a registered custom property is never composited (UnsupportedCSSProperty: --angle). Two cards cost 152 ms/s of main thread (vs 0.5 idle), 60 style recalcs/s and ~180 paints/s, continuously, for as long as the loop runs. That is the single most expensive "safe-looking" effect in the inventory.
guidance: Do not run @property angle animations as ambient loops. Use the rotated conic pseudo-element below for ambient borders.
Acceptable on :hover/:focus-visible only (bounded, T0/T1), or as a static conic border.

effects.name: Conic gradient border via transform-rotated conic layer (alternative to @property, 2 elements)
effects.notes: Same look: an oversized conic-gradient child (inset:-50%) rotated with transform inside the card (overflow:hidden) with an inner surface pseudo-element 2 px in. 3.6 ms/s, 0 of 2 failed to composite, 0.6 paints/s, 0 long frames. Compositor cost ~130 ms/s software at 412 px.
guidance: Keep it to <=2 ambient elements per page (budget: infinite animations per viewport <= 8); pause off-screen.

effects.name: Glass bento: backdrop-filter blur(16px) over a STATIC background (6 cards)
effects.lighthouseNote: Not run separately (static glass adds no main-thread work during load).
effects.notes: Idle cost is zero (0.6 ms/s; nothing redraws). While scrolling the main thread matches the plain page (49 vs 47 ms/s) but the compositor re-blurs every glass card on every scroll frame: 181 ms/s vs 28 ms/s software-compositor CPU on the same scroll (6.5x).
guidance: <=3 backdrop-filter elements per mobile viewport (budget), blur <=16px, contrast-safe alpha, solid fallback under prefers-reduced-transparency / prefers-contrast: more / no support.

effects.name: Glass bento: backdrop-filter blur(16px) over an ANIMATED background (6 cards over drifting layers)
effects.lighthouseNote: Delta vs baseline; Lighthouse cannot see compositor cost, so expect ~0.
effects.notes: Main thread is unaffected (4.6 vs 4.4 ms/s for identical solid cards over the same drifting layers) but every frame re-blurs every card: software-compositor CPU 643 vs 152 ms/s at 412 px (4.2x), and at 1440x900 the frame rate falls from 55 to 42 fps. Low-end phones pay this on the GPU every frame.
guidance: No backdrop-filter over animated layers at any width: use solid or pre-tinted cards over living art, or pause the layers behind glass. Glass is fine over static art.

effects.name: Cross-document view transitions (@view-transition navigation:auto, header + h1 named, 0.25 s)
effects.lighthouseNote: n/a: Lighthouse measures a cold load, where no view transition runs. CSS ~0.2 KB.
effects.notes: Per same-origin navigation (trace, mobile, 4x): 337 ms main-thread vs 203 ms without (+134 ms), +188 ms software-compositor; new-page FCP 140 ms vs 96 ms (rendering is held for the snapshot); transition finished ~390 ms after navigation start; 7 long animation frames in 9 navigations vs 1, but total blocking duration only ~4 ms. All 15 transition animations ran on the main thread (UnsupportedCSSProperty for the UA width/height group animations, AnimationHasNoVisibleChange for the unchanged header), so the 250 ms transition is main-thread work. It is bounded (T1) and invisible to Lighthouse.
effects.measuredOn: vt-navigation on mobile (412x823), action=nav, baseline=novt-navigation (navigation: main-thread figures from the trace, getMetrics resets per document)
guidance: Name <=3 elements (header, page title); never name the living-art layers or large images (each name is a snapshot).
Duration <=250 ms; inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); animation:none under [data-motion=off].

effects.name: Living CTA band: 3 pre-blurred radial-gradient blobs moved by transform
effects.notes: 2.9 ms/s main thread, 0 of 3 failed, 60 fps, 0.8 paints/s, 143 ms/s software-compositor at 412 px. This is the reference for the filter:blur negative control: same look, ~7x less compositor work and no dropped frames.
guidance: Gradients baked into the blob (radial-gradient to transparent), transform only, fixed scrim under the text, pause off-screen.

effects.name: Static grain overlay (692 B PNG data-URI tile at 5% on deep bands)
effects.lighthouseNote: Included in the all-safe page; ~1 KB of CSS.
effects.notes: No measurable cost: scrolling with grain is within noise of the plain page, and grain over the animated CTA blobs does not change the blob numbers (3.4 vs 2.9 ms/s, same compositor load). The feTurbulence SVG tile variant (462 chars) also measured flat, because the tile is rasterised once.
guidance: Static only (never animate the grain or use background-attachment: fixed); no blend modes; removed under prefers-contrast and forced-colors.

effects.name: Map glow: drop-shadow filter on hover/focus of SVG tiles (transitioned) and ambient pulse on the current area
effects.lighthouseNote: Hover never runs in Lighthouse; the pulse variants were not run separately.
effects.notes: Hover sweep across all 13 tiles with a 0.2 s filter transition: 167 ms/s vs 96 ms/s for the same sweep without the glow (+72 ms/s), ~59 style recalcs/s and ~90 paints/s (FilterRelatedPropertyMayMovePixels, filter on an SVG child is not composited). Ambient pulse by animating drop-shadow on the current tile: 76 ms/s continuously with 60 recalcs/s (avoid). Ambient pulse as an HTML glow box over the map animated by opacity: 3.4 ms/s, composited (safe).
guidance: Hover/focus: switch the drop-shadow on instantly (no filter transition); transition fill/stroke only (T0 <=200 ms).
Ambient pulse on the current area: an aria-hidden HTML (or outer <svg>) glow box positioned over the tile and animated by opacity, never an animated filter on the polygon.

effects.name: NEGATIVE control: filter: blur(64px) blobs moved by transform

lighthouseDelta.page: neg-both: inner-node CSS + filter:blur blobs (alive immediately)

effects.lighthouseNote: Combined with the inner-node CSS control; Lighthouse cannot see compositor cost.
effects.notes: Confirms the rule. The animation itself composites (0 of 3 failed, 3.5 ms/s main thread), so a main-thread-only audit would pass it, but the compositor must re-blur three large layers every frame: 981 ms/s software-compositor CPU (vs 143 for pre-blurred gradients), and the frame rate falls to 43 fps at 412 px and 21 fps at 1440x900.
guidance: Use pre-blurred radial-gradient blobs. filter: blur() on moving or large elements is banned.

effects.name: NEGATIVE control: inner-node SVG animation, CSS transform/opacity on <g>/<circle> inside one SVG

lighthouseDelta.page: neg-both: inner-node CSS + filter:blur blobs (alive immediately)

effects.notes: Unexpected result: Chromium 153 composited the CSS transform/opacity animations on the 5 inner <g> layers and 12 firefly circles (0 of 17 failed on desktop; on mobile 8 of 17 were skipped as AnimationHasNoVisibleChange because those nodes were cropped out of the narrow viewport; no per-frame paints), costing 6.5 ms/s, about the same as the outer-box version. This lab could not test WebKit (all iOS browsers), which does not composite animations on SVG child elements; there the whole SVG repaints every frame. So the outer-box rule is still right for cross-engine reasons, even though Chromium does not penalise this.
guidance: Keep the outer-box rule for the hero and anything large. Small accents (a few firefly circles) inside a small SVG are tolerable in Chromium but untested in WebKit.

effects.name: NEGATIVE control: inner-node SVG animation via SMIL (<animateTransform>/<animate>)
effects.notes: 218 ms/s main thread (vs 4.8 for the same scene as outer boxes), ~720 style recalcs/s and 120 paints/s, continuously. SMIL never composites.
guidance: Banned for anything ambient.

effects.name: NEGATIVE control: inner-node SVG animation via JS requestAnimationFrame writing attributes
effects.notes: 207 ms/s main thread, 60 style recalcs/s, 120 paints/s, continuously (plus the rAF loop keeps the main thread producing frames). The pattern most animation libraries use for SVG.
guidance: Banned: no JS-driven per-frame animation; living.js only toggles classes and play-state.

effects.name: COMBINED safe set (all-safe page: hero layers + fireflies, parallax wrapper, view() reveals, rotated conic x2, CTA blobs + grain, contour one-shot, map hover glow, spotlight, view transitions)
effects.lighthouseNote: Perf 100 either way; Lighthouse lists the 12 contour paths as non-composited and its main-thread work rises by ~700 ms, but TBT median stays 0 (worst single run 36 ms).
effects.notes: Steady state with every ambient loop running and nothing scrolling: 1.3 ms/s main thread, 0 style recalcs, 0 paints, 0 long frames: the ambient layer is free on the main thread. The first 5 s after start-up cost 97 ms/s, almost all from the 12-path contour draw-in (non-composited). While scrolling, the scroll-linked effects add up: 178 ms/s vs 47 ms/s on the plain page (+131 ms/s, ~78 style recalcs/s, still 0 long frames). Software-compositor load is ~260 ms/s at 412 px and saturates at 1440x900 (51 fps) in this GPU-less container.
guidance: Ambient (T2) loops built from transform/opacity on outer boxes are effectively free on the main thread; spend the budget there.
Scroll-linked (T4) effects are where the main-thread cost is: keep parallax to the hero and do reveals with the one-shot IntersectionObserver pattern.
Trigger the contour draw-in only when the map enters view, never at start-up together with everything else.
